# Data preparation
```{r} 
# across all variables in data preparation, shared manipulations comprise 1) reading the relevent NHANES table from the nhanesdata R package and 2) subsetting the data to the 2015 survey cycle to reflect project scope where the variable seqn reflects participant IDs and the variable year indicates the survey cycle
```

## Statins

```{r}
rxq_rx  <-
  read_nhanes("rxq_rx") %>% # table: rxq_rx , Prescription Medications data file
  clean_names() %>% # standardize text for regex
  filter(year == 2015) %>%
  mutate(
    statins_use    = as.integer(str_detect(rxddrug, regex('atorvastatin|simvastatin|fluvastatin|lovastatin|
                                             pitavastatin|pravastatin|rosuvastatin', ignore_case = T))), # identify statin use using regular expressions
  ) %>%
  select(year, seqn, statins_use, rxddays) %>% # extract relevant data mapping statin use across time (rxddays = Number of days taken medicine, year) and participant ID (seqn)
  group_by(year, seqn) %>%
  summarise(
    statin = as.integer(any(statins_use == 1, na.rm = TRUE)), # create treatment variable where a participant is included if any of their prescriptsion are a statin

    statin_days = ifelse(
      any(statins_use == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
      max(rxddays[statins_use == 1], na.rm = TRUE),
      NA_real_
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) # establish the length of time in treatement given the maximum number of days taking a statin medication
table(rxq_rx$statin) # examine distribution of treatment in the full 2015 data
```

```{r}
# use to filter previous diagnosis of hypercholesterolemia
bpq<- read_nhanes("bpq") %>%  # table: bpq, Blood Pressure & Cholesterol data file
  filter(year == 2015) %>%
  select(year,seqn,bpq080) %>% # bpq080: Doctor told you - high cholesterol level
  filter(bpq080 == "Yes") # extract relevant data of participants with a history of high cholestorol

# final exposure data --> all data have to fit this
exposure_df<-
bpq %>%
  left_join(rxq_rx) # create treatment data, which only includes participants who have a clinical diagnosis of high cholesterol and includes the treatment indicator of 0 (control) or 1 (exposure)
```

## CVD and mortality

```{r}
mcq     <- read_nhanes("mcq") # table: mcq, Medical Conditions data file

cvd <- mcq %>%
  filter(year == 2015) %>%
  select(seqn, year, mcq160e, mcq180e) %>% # mcq160e: Ever told you had heart attack, mcq180e: Age when told you had heart attack
  mutate(
    heart_attack = ifelse(mcq160e == "Yes", 1, 0), # create an outcome indicator of 0 (no heart attack diagnosis) or 1 (prior heart attack diagnosis)
    age_first_ha = mcq180e # create a variable indicating the participant's age of heart attack diagnosis
  ) %>%
  select(year, seqn, heart_attack, age_first_ha) # extract relevant heart attack data

# Final data exposure + outcome
final_df<-
  exposure_df %>%
  left_join(cvd) # add participant's relevant heart attack outcome data to the treatment data to create final data
```

## Confounders

```{r}
# Age, gender, Income, edu level
demo_conf <-
  read_nhanes("demo") %>% # table: demo, Demographic Variables
  select(year, seqn, ridageyr, riagendr, dmdeduc2, indfmpir) %>% # ridageyr: Age at Screening, riagendr: Gender, with Non-Hispanic Asian Category, dmdeduc2: Education level - Adults 20+, indfmpir: Ratio of family income to poverty
  filter(year == 2015) %>%
  mutate(
    dmdeduc2 = case_when(
      dmdeduc2 == "Less than 9th grade" ~ "less_than_9th",
      dmdeduc2 == "9-11th grade (Includes 12th grade with no diploma)" ~ "9th_to_11th",
      dmdeduc2 == "High school graduate/GED or equivalent" ~ "high_school",
      dmdeduc2 == "Some college or AA degree" ~ "some_college",
      dmdeduc2 == "College graduate or above" ~ "college_or_above",
      dmdeduc2 %in% c("Don't know", "Refused") ~ NA_character_,
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ), # simply education naming conventions

    dmdeduc2 = factor(
      dmdeduc2,
      levels = c(
        "less_than_9th",
        "9th_to_11th",
        "high_school",
        "some_college",
        "college_or_above"
      ),
      ordered = TRUE
    ) # classify recoded education as ordinal
  ) %>%
  rename(
    age = ridageyr,
    gender = riagendr,
    education = dmdeduc2,
    income = indfmpir
  ) # simply variable names

# Diet
diet_conf<-
  read_nhanes("dbq") %>% # table: dbq, Diet Behavior & Nutrition
  filter(year == 2015) %>%
  select(year,seqn,dbq700) %>% # dbq700: How healthy is the diet
  rename(
    diet = dbq700
  ) # simply variable name

# High blood pressure
bloodpress_conf<-
  read_nhanes("bpq") %>% # table: bpq, Blood Pressure & Cholesterol
  filter(year == 2015) %>%
  select(year,seqn,bpq020) %>% # bpq020: ever told you had high blood pressure
  rename(
    hypertension = bpq020
  ) # simply variable name

# Diabetes / blood sugar
diabetes_conf<-
  read_nhanes("ghb") %>% # table: ghb, Glycohemoglobin
  filter(year == 2015) %>%
  mutate(
    blood_sugar = ifelse(lbxgh >=6.5,1,0) # lbxgh: Glycohemoglobin, set diabetes indicator to 1 if glycohemoglobin exceeds 6.5 A1C threshold for diabetes, 0 if not
  ) %>%
  select(
    year,seqn,blood_sugar
  ) # select relevant participant blood_sugar content

# Serum Cholesterol
chol_conf<-
  read_nhanes("tchol") %>% # table: tchol, Cholesterol - Total
  filter(year == 2015) %>%
  rename(
    cholesterol = lbxtc # simplify variable name for lbxtc: Total Cholesterol (mg/dL)
  ) %>%
  select(
    year,seqn,cholesterol
  )

# bmi
imc_conf<-
  read_nhanes("bmx") %>% # table: bmx, Body Measures
  select(
    year,seqn,bmxbmi # extract relevant participant bmi data, bmi: Body Mass Index (kg/m**2)
  ) %>%
  filter(
    year == 2015
  )   %>% rename(
    bmi = bmxbmi
  ) # simply variable name

# Smoking status
smoking_comf <-
  read_nhanes("smq") %>%  # table: smq, Smoking - Cigarette Use
  filter(
    year == 2015
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    smoking_status = case_when( # smq020: # Smoked at least 100 cigarettes in life, smq040: Do you now smoke cigarettes?
      smq020 == "No" ~ 0, # Never
      smq020=="Yes" & smq040=="Not at all" ~ 1, # Former
      smq020=="Yes" & smq040 %in% c("Every day","Some days") ~ 2, # Current
      T ~ NA
    ) # recode to simply as non-smoker, former smoker or current smoker
  ) %>%
  select(year,seqn,smoking_status) # extract relevant participant smoking status data

# Physical activity
phys_conf<-
  read_nhanes("paq") %>% # table: paq, Physical Activity
  filter(year ==2015) %>%
  select(year,seqn, pad680) %>% # extract extract relevant participant physical activity data, pad680: minutes sedentary activity

# Health insurance

  read_nhanes("hiq") %>% # table: hiq, Health Insurance

  select(
```

## Final data

```{r}
df_work<-
  final_df %>% # add participant's relevant covariate data to final dataframe
  left_join(demo_conf) %>%
  left_join(bloodpress_conf) %>%
  left_join(diabetes_conf) %>%
  left_join(chol_conf) %>%
  left_join(imc_conf) %>%
  left_join(smoking_comf) %>%
  left_join(phys_conf) %>%
  left_join(insurance_conf) %>%
  left_join(proximity_conf) %>%
  left_join(diet_conf) %>%

  mutate(
    statin_start = age-(statin_days/365), # approximate age of statin initiaiton
    heart_attack_incident = case_when(
      statin == 1 ~ as.integer(heart_attack == 1 & age_first_ha > statin_start),
      statin == 0 ~ heart_attack,
      TRUE        ~ NA_integer_
    ) # adjust treatment indicator so that only statin use that preceeds a heart attack diagnosis is considered
  ) %>%
  filter(
    !health_insurance %in% c("Don't know","Refused"),
    diet != "Don't know"
  ) %>% # exclude respondents with vague or missing data on covariates
  mutate(
    statin = as.factor(statin),
    education = as.numeric(factor(education)) # convert treatment to binary factor and education to numeric for evaluation
  )

write.csv(df_work,"df_work.csv",row.names = F) # create data file
```


```{r}
df_work_age_filter<-
  df_work %>%
  filter(
    age > 50
  ) # subset the final data to only include older adults
```

# Dataset: We use the age > 50 dataset for our estimation
```{r}
# age-filtered (age > 50) and imputed the dataset.
df_work_exp_age_filter <- df_work_age_filter %>%  select(statin,bmi,age,education,health_insurance,physical_activity,gender)

# Perform multiple imputation using predictive mean matching (PMM)
# to address missing covariate values while preserving plausible
# observed data distributions.
imp <- mice(df_work_exp_age_filter, m = 5, method = "pmm", seed = 123)

# Imputed datasets
df1 <- complete(imp, 1) 
df2 <- complete(imp, 2)
df3 <- complete(imp, 3)
df4 <- complete(imp, 4)
df5 <- complete(imp, 5)
```


# Estimation

## Estimation 1
## Use standarization to find the risk ratio
```{r}
g_formula_function <- function(data, formula){ # g-computation estimator returning RR with 95% CI via percentile bootstrap

  model_adj <- glm(formula, data = data, family = binomial) # fit outcome model adjusted for covariates in formula

model_a1 <- predict(model_adj, newdata = data %>% mutate(statin = factor(1, levels = levels(statin))), type = "response") # predicted P(Y=1|A=1, L) under universal treatment
model_a0 <- predict(model_adj, newdata = data %>% mutate(statin = factor(0, levels = levels(statin))), type = "response") # predicted P(Y=1|A=0, L) under universal control

estimate <- mean(model_a1, na.rm = T) / mean(model_a0, na.rm = T) # marginal risk ratio: E[Y(1)] / E[Y(0)]

ate_statin <- function(data, indx) { # bootstrap resampling function for ATE estimation

  d <- data[indx, ]

  model_Y <- glm(formula, data = d, family = binomial) # refit outcome model on bootstrap sample

  d1 <- d %>% mutate(statin  = factor(1, levels = levels(statin))) # counterfactual: everyone treated

  d0 <- d %>% mutate(statin  = factor(0, levels = levels(statin))) # counterfactual: no one treated

  Y_a_1 <- predict(model_Y, newdata = d1, type = "response")
  Y_a_0 <- predict(model_Y, newdata = d0, type = "response")

  ate <- mean(Y_a_1, na.rm = T)/ mean(Y_a_0, na.rm = T) # bootstrap RR estimate

  return(ate)
}

boot_ate_statin <- boot::boot(data = data, statistic = ate_statin, R = 999) # run 999 bootstrap iterations

#boot_ate_smoke$t0
ic_ate <- quantile(boot_ate_statin$t, c(.025,.975)) # percentile 95% CI

return(list(
    RR = estimate,
    CI = ic_ate
  ))

}
```

## Formula 1: with bmi and df_work age-filtered
```{r}
stdr_bmi <- g_formula_function(data = df_work_age_filter, formula = heart_attack_incident ~ statin  + bmi + age + education + health_insurance + physical_activity + gender)
stdr_bmi
```

```{r}
stdr_nobmi
```

# Estimation 2
## Use IPW to find the risk ratio
```{r}
# Pool treatment effect estimates across the 5 imputed datasets
# using Rubin's rules to account for both within-imputation and
# between-imputation variability.
get_pooled <- function(estimates, ses) {
  m  <- length(estimates)
  Q  <- mean(estimates)
  W  <- mean(ses^2)
  B  <- var(estimates)
  SE <- sqrt(W + (1 + 1/m) * B)
  c(Estimate = round(Q, 4), SE = round(SE, 4),
    CI_lower  = round(Q - 1.96 * SE, 4),
    CI_upper  = round(Q + 1.96 * SE, 4))
}
```



```{r}
# IPW estimates returning log(RR) and SE(logRR) for age > 50
ipw_mice <- function(data, data2, formula, trim = NULL) {

  data$heart_attack_incident <- data2$heart_attack_incident

  model_ps <- glm(formula,
                  data = data,
                  family = binomial)

  data$ps <- predict(model_ps,
                     type = "response")

  if (!is.null(trim))
    data <- data %>%
      filter(ps >= trim &
             ps <= (1 - trim))

  p_statin <- mean(data$statin == 1,
                   na.rm = TRUE)

  data <- data %>%
    mutate(
      w_stab = case_when(
        statin == 1 ~ p_statin / ps,
        statin == 0 ~ (1 - p_statin) / (1 - ps),
        TRUE ~ NA_real_
      )
    )

  model <- glm(
    heart_attack_incident ~ statin,
    data = data,
    weights = w_stab,
    family = binomial(link = "log")
  )

  c(
    est = unname(coef(model)["statin1"]),
    se  = unname(
      sqrt(vcov(model)["statin1",
                       "statin1"])
    )
  )
}
```


```{r, warning=F}
#IPW for each imputed dataset
#with bmi
ipw_res <- map_df(
  .x = list(df1,df2,df3,df4,df5),
  .f = ~ipw_mice(data = .x, formula = statin ~ bmi + age + education + health_insurance + physical_activity + gender, data2 = df_work_age_filter)
) # apply IPW across all 5 imputed datasets

ipw_bmi <- get_pooled(ipw_res$est, ipw_res$se) # pool estimates with Rubin's rules
exp(ipw_bmi[c("Estimate","CI_lower","CI_upper")]) # report risk ratio
```


```{r, warning=F}
#without bmi
ipw_res2 <- map_df(
  .x = list(df1,df2,df3,df4,df5),
  .f = ~ipw_mice(data = .x, formula = statin ~ age + education + health_insurance + physical_activity + gender, data2 = df_work_age_filter)
) # apply IPW across all 5 imputed datasets, excluding bmi from propensity model

ipw_nobmi <- get_pooled(ipw_res2$est, ipw_res2$se) # pool estimates with Rubin's rules
exp(ipw_nobmi[c("Estimate","CI_lower","CI_upper")]) # report risk ratio
```

```{r}
#without bmi and trimmed
ipw_res3 <- map_df(
  .x = list(df1,df2,df3,df4,df5),
  .f = ~ipw_mice(data = .x, trim = 0.3, formula = statin ~ age + education + health_insurance + physical_activity + gender, data2 = df_work_age_filter)
) # apply IPW with propensity score trimming at 0.3 to address near-violations of positivity

ipw_trim <- get_pooled(ipw_res3$est, ipw_res3$se) # pool estimates with Rubin's rules
exp(ipw_trim[c("Estimate","CI_lower","CI_upper")]) # report risk ratio
```

# Estimation 3
## Use AIPW to find the risk ratio
```{r}
get_aipw <- function(data, outcome, formula, ps_formula) { # doubly-robust AIPW estimator; consistent if either the outcome model or propensity score model is correctly specified

  data$heart_attack_incident <- outcome # attach outcome from original (pre-imputation) data

  model_Y  <- glm(formula,    data = data, family = binomial) # outcome model
  model_ps <- glm(ps_formula, data = data, family = binomial) # propensity score model

  ps_hat <- predict(model_ps, type = "response") # estimated propensity scores
  
  d1 <- data %>% mutate(statin = factor(1, levels = levels(data$statin))) 
  d0 <- data %>% mutate(statin = factor(0, levels = levels(data$statin))) 

  mu1 <- predict(model_Y, newdata = d1, type = "response") # predicted outcome under treatment
  mu0 <- predict(model_Y, newdata = d0, type = "response") # predicted outcome under control

  A <- as.numeric(as.character(data$statin))
  Y <- data$heart_attack_incident

  eif1 <- mu1 + A       * (Y - mu1) / ps_hat        # efficient influence function for E[Y(1)]
  eif0 <- mu0 + (1 - A) * (Y - mu0) / (1 - ps_hat)  # efficient influence function for E[Y(0)]

  p1 <- mean(eif1, na.rm = TRUE) # AIPW estimate of E[Y(1)]
  p0 <- mean(eif0, na.rm = TRUE) # AIPW estimate of E[Y(0)]
  n  <- sum(!is.na(eif1) & !is.na(eif0))

  if_rr <- eif1 / p0 - p1 * eif0 / p0^2 # delta-method influence function for the RR

  c(est = p1 / p0,
    se  = sd(if_rr, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n)) # return RR and SE derived from influence function
}
```

## AIPW with bmi
```{r}
aipw_res <- map_df(
  .x = list(df1,df2,df3,df4,df5),
  .f = ~get_aipw(
    data       = .x,
    outcome    = df_work_age_filter$heart_attack_incident,
    formula    = heart_attack_incident ~ statin + bmi + age + education + health_insurance + physical_activity + gender,
    ps_formula = statin ~ bmi + age + education + health_insurance + physical_activity + gender
  )
) # apply AIPW across all 5 imputed datasets

aipw_bmi <- get_pooled(aipw_res$est, aipw_res$se) # pool RR estimates 
aipw_bmi
```

## AIPW without bmi: no BMI - this estimator is for the primary analysis of AIPW with the initial adjustment set
```{r}
aipw_res2 <- map_df(
  .x = list(df1,df2,df3,df4,df5),
  .f = ~get_aipw(
    data       = .x,
    outcome    = df_work_age_filter$heart_attack_incident,
    formula    = heart_attack_incident ~ statin + age + education + health_insurance + physical_activity + gender,
    ps_formula = statin ~ age + education + health_insurance + physical_activity + gender
  )
) # apply AIPW across all 5 imputed datasets, excluding bmi from both models

aipw_nobmi <- get_pooled(aipw_res2$est, aipw_res2$se) # pool RR estimates 
aipw_nobmi
```

```{r}
summary_table <- data.frame(
  method   = c("stdr_bmi","stdr_nobmi","IPW_bmi","IPW_nobmi","IPW_trim","AIPW_bmi","AIPW_nobmi"),
  estimate = round(c(stdr_bmi$RR, stdr_nobmi$RR, exp(ipw_bmi["Estimate"]), exp(ipw_nobmi["Estimate"]), exp(ipw_trim["Estimate"]), aipw_bmi["Estimate"], aipw_nobmi["Estimate"]), 3),
  low      = round(c(stdr_bmi$CI[1], stdr_nobmi$CI[1], exp(ipw_bmi["CI_lower"]), exp(ipw_nobmi["CI_lower"]), exp(ipw_trim["CI_lower"]), aipw_bmi["CI_lower"], aipw_nobmi["CI_lower"]), 3),
  upper    = round(c(stdr_bmi$CI[2], stdr_nobmi$CI[2], exp(ipw_bmi["CI_upper"]), exp(ipw_nobmi["CI_upper"]), exp(ipw_trim["CI_upper"]), aipw_bmi["CI_upper"], aipw_nobmi["CI_upper"]), 3),
  row.names = NULL
) # compile RR point estimates and 95% CIs across all estimation methods

```

```{r}
summary_table %>%
  mutate(
    type = str_detect(method, pattern = "nobmi"),     # flag models excluding bmi
    type_est = ifelse(str_detect(method, pattern = "^stdr"),1,
                      ifelse(str_detect(method, pattern = "^AIPW"),2,
                             ifelse(str_detect(method, pattern = "^IPW"),3,NA))), # classify estimation method for faceting: 1=standardization, 2=AIPW, 3=IPW

    type_est = as.factor(type_est)
    ) %>%
  ggplot() +
  geom_pointrange(aes(x = estimate, y = method, xmin = low, xmax = upper, col = type)) +
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept = 1),linetype = "dashed") + # reference line at RR = 1 (null effect)
  facet_grid(type_est ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") + # separate panels by estimation method

  theme_classic() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    strip.text = element_blank()
  )

ggsave("./fig1.png", dpi = 300, bg = "white") # save forest plot
```

# Sensitivity analysis

## E-values

```{r}
# E-values computed using the OR formulation with rare=TRUE,
# which approximates RR for relatively rare outcomes.

summary_table %>%
  group_by(method) %>%
  nest() %>%
  mutate(
    Evalue = map(.x = data,
                 .f = ~evalues.RR(est = .x$estimate, lo = .x$low, hi = .x$upper)), # compute E-value for each method's RR estimate

    Evalue_est = map_dbl(.x = Evalue,
                     .f =  ~.x[2,1]), # E-value for point estimate

    Evalue_ci = map_dbl(.x = Evalue,
                     .f =  ~.x[2,3]) # E-value for CI bound closest to null
    ) %>%

  unnest(data) %>%
  select(method, estimate, low, upper, Evalue_est, Evalue_ci)
```
```{r}
ls("package:EValue")
```

# Diagnostics:
## Diagnostics 1: Propensity overlap to check propensity score overlaping for 
## treatment and control group before and after weighting in IPW with the first 
## imputated dataset based on the dataset filtered by age > 50.
```{r}
# Use first imputed dataset for diagnostics
# Use propensity overlap to examine common support (overlap) between treated and
# untreated groups. Lack of overlap may indicate positivity violations and
# unstable IPW estimates.
df_diag <- df1

model_ps_diag <- glm(
  statin ~ age + education + gender + health_insurance + physical_activity,
  data = df_diag,
  family = binomial
)

df_diag$ps <- predict(
  model_ps_diag,
  type = "response"
)

p_statin <- mean(df_diag$statin == 1)

df_diag <- df_diag %>%
  mutate(
    w_stab = case_when(
      statin == 1 ~ p_statin / ps,
      statin == 0 ~ (1 - p_statin) / (1 - ps)
    )
  )

# Before weighting
ggplot(
  df_diag,
  aes(
    x = ps,
    fill = statin
  )
) +
  geom_histogram(
    position = "identity",
    alpha = 0.4,
    bins = 30
  ) +

  labs(
    title = "Propensity Score Distribution Before Weighting (Age > 50)",
    x = "Propensity Score",
    y = "Count"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```


```{r}
# After weighting
ggplot(
  df_diag,
  aes(
    x = ps,
    fill = statin,
    weight = w_stab
  )
) +
  geom_histogram(
    position = "identity",
    alpha = 0.4,
    bins = 30
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Propensity Score Distribution After Weighting (Age > 50)",
    x = "Propensity Score",
    y = "Weighted Count"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Diagnostics 2: Love plot to check covariate balance before and after IPW
## using df1 (df_diag) after age trimming (age > 50).
```{r}
# Covariate balance
library(cobalt)

bal_ipw <- bal.tab(
  statin ~ age + education + gender + health_insurance + physical_activity,
  data = df_diag,
  weights = df_diag$w_stab,
  method = "weighting",
  un = TRUE
)

bal_ipw$Balance
```

```{r}
# Draw love plot
love.plot(
  bal_ipw,
  stats = "mean.diffs",
  abs = TRUE,
  threshold = 0.1,
  var.order = "unadjusted"
)+
  labs(
    title = "Covariate Balance Before and After IPW (Age > 50)"
  ) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)
  )

```
